clue.text: Moved in a body like some pupils

definitions.meaning: to flow along together as a crowd or current does
British schools sort pupils into ability groups called streams, so such pupils have been grouped this way

explanation.surface: A crowd of schoolchildren surges along together.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd pouring along has flowed en masse, and pupils placed in ability sets at a British school have been divided the same way.

clue.text: 6 ac makes a Welshman no end fed up

indicators.note: no end means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Taffy is a nickname for a Welshman

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: having fed means one ate

explanation.surface: A Welshman, utterly sick of it, produces some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: '6 ac' refers to the answer at 6 across, a material. 'no end' trims TAFFY to TAFF; 'up' turns ATE into ETA.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp lustrous silk or rayon weave is a kind of textile.

clue.text: Come across a totter-up of print units

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of measurement
one who tots up figures is a counter

explanation.surface: To meet someone who adds up printers' measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' sets the ens after the counter in the clue, but in the answer they come first: a counter of ens.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet by chance is to bump into someone unexpectedly.

clue.text: Copper, say, possibly showing such courage

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken that sounds like another

parts.note: copper is a metal

explanation.surface: A police officer, perhaps, displaying bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer, who might well show courage, but it is the metal; 'possibly showing such' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit and pluck; the word began as a spelling variant of the material word.

clue.text: Cleveland's popular form of entertainment?

parts.note: reads as a well-liked kind of social gathering, but Grover Cleveland was a US president of one of the two main political organisations

explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland led the American political group named for rule by the people, read as a jolly gathering open to all.

clue.text: Substance of footballers' 19, almost

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, the body governing English footballers

indicators.note: almost means the word is left one letter short of complete

parts.note: the answer to 19 across is a blunder, and dropping a brick is a British idiom for such a blunder

explanation.surface: The heart of what footballers' blunder amounts to, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' points to the faux pas at 19 across; a BRICK is the British word for a tactless blunder. 'almost' drops its last letter, K, leaving BRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric can mean the basic structure or material of something, as in the fabric of society.

clue.text: Last five characters for a play season

indicators.note: the characters, meaning letters, of the words are used for something new by rearrangement

explanation.surface: The final five roles in a drama series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like roles in a play, but it means the letters of LAST FIVE, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An arts gala of drama, like Edinburgh's, is a concentrated season of performances.

clue.text: Debauchee accepts money — it's the regular thing

indicators.note: accepts means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: a roué is a dissolute man, a rake
tin is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A libertine takes cash: that's normal practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A set habitual practice is the usual procedure.

clue.text: Allowed a man in the City to raise customers

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means reading the whole from bottom to top
in means the words before it are put inside the district

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London
let means allowed
Neil is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man permitted into London's financial district boosts the patrons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to raise' turns the whole assembly upwards, since this is a down clue; the City of London's postal code is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of patrons of a shop or firm.

clue.text: Discontinued fashion surviving in the timber yard

definitions.note: described as a leftover remnant piece lying in a wood yard

parts.note: a dish that is off has been withdrawn from the menu, so discontinued
to fashion is to shape, as a tailor cuts cloth

explanation.surface: A style no longer made lingers on among the planks of a timber merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover scrap of wood after sawing is a remnant, which is what lies about a sawmill.

clue.text: State of a single Cockney nymph

parts.note: an unmarried woman is addressed as Miss

indicators.note: London Cockney speech famously drops the initial letter H of words

parts.note: a houri is a beautiful maiden of the Islamic paradise, a nymph

explanation.surface: The situation of an unmarried London nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney' drops the H of HOURI, giving OURI.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state on the Mississippi, named after a native people.

clue.text: The equal society — something surviving round the inn

indicators.note: round means the first word wraps itself about the second

parts.note: a relic is a thing surviving from the past
a pub is a British inn or tavern

explanation.surface: An egalitarian community whose only heirloom stands around the local tavern.
explanation.definitionFit: A state with no monarch is held up as a society of equal citizens, a commonwealth.

clue.text: Exotic and swinging, such clubs!

definitions.meaning: from a faraway land in the East, such as the subcontinent
bottle-shaped wooden clubs swung in Victorian gymnastics exercises bear this name

explanation.definitionFit: Something from the subcontinent once seemed foreign and strange to Britons, and the bowling-pin-shaped exercise clubs swung for fitness carry this name.

clue.text: A sot's treatment in drying-out establishments

indicators.note: giving the words treatment works them over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A drunkard is sent to rehab clinics to dry out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drying-out' suggests alcohol rehab for the sot, but these are kilns for drying hops.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilns for drying hops are buildings where hops are dried, a cryptic twist on rehab clinics.

clue.text: Incompetent fellow used to stop the train!

definitions.meaning: read as a former device that halts carriages, a railway buffer of old

explanation.definitionFit: A fuddy-duddy past his best is one sense; a buffer that once halted rail wagons is the punning second.

clue.text: Ornament to obstruct part of a play

parts.note: to dam a river is to block it
a scene is one division of a play, given here with its article

explanation.surface: Decoration meant to hold up a section of a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: To damascene metal is to decorate it with inlaid gold or silver patterns, as Damascus smiths did.

clue.text: Attractive bit of stuff on board?

definitions.meaning: British slang 'a bit of ...' means an attractive woman
the crisp roast pork rind is carved on a board

explanation.definitionFit: Dated British slang calls an attractive woman a bit of this, and it is also crisp roast pork skin served at a carving table.

clue.text: Fighter with a hot temper

definitions.meaning: the Second World War RAF fighter plane
a fiery, quick-tempered person, given adjectivally

explanation.definitionFit: The famous British warplane of 1940, and a fiery person quick to flare up.

clue.text: Bad condition of traveller in Underworld atmosphere

indicators.note: in means the first-named piece is set inside the others

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for Hades itself
air is the atmosphere around us
a rep is a commercial traveller, a sales representative

explanation.surface: The poor state of a voyager lost in the gloomy air of Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilapidation, a building or object having fallen into a poor state for want of upkeep.

clue.text: Old frock-coat or overall for a Frenchman

definitions.meaning: a man's long close-fitting overcoat of past centuries
the French phrase ... means over all

explanation.definitionFit: A historical man's overcoat, whose name is French for above everything.

clue.text: Old fellow endlessly making faux pas

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut away

parts.note: a gaffer is an old man in British dialect, or a boss

explanation.surface: An elderly chap keeps on committing social blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: A social blunder or tactless slip, which the French phrase names.

clue.text: Flower, profuse on a lost Continent

parts.note: free can mean lavish or profuse

indicators.note: lost means the following letter has gone missing from the word

parts.note: Asia is a continent

explanation.surface: Blooms grow abundantly on Atlantis, the sunken continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lost Continent' suggests Atlantis, but 'a' is the letter dropped from ASIA, leaving SIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant South African bloom of the iris family.

clue.text: A don has it to his advantage

parts.note: a prof is a professor, a university don

explanation.surface: A university lecturer turns something to his own benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gain or benefit, as in to one's profit.

clue.text: The outcome of peacekeepers' holiday?

parts.note: the UN sends peacekeeping forces to troubled areas
a rest is a break or holiday

explanation.surface: What happens when the blue helmets go on leave?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: with the UN troops off on a break, trouble follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Disturbance and agitation is exactly what breaks out once the keepers of order are away.

clue.text: Noisy bird disrupts karate and PE

indicators.note: disrupting breaks the letters up into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A screeching bird interrupts a martial arts session and a gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: A small long-tailed parrot, a squawking cage bird.

clue.text: Promenade that's right for a border

parts.note: the seafront is the promenade at a British resort
ie is the abbreviation of the Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: The seaside walkway works fine as a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: The line dividing one country from another is its boundary.

clue.text: Weak, but knowing about one piece of writing

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the others

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or knowing
I is the Roman numeral one
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: Feeble, though wise to a certain document.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insubstantial or easily torn is frail, as an excuse or fabric can be.

clue.text: Withdraw and adorn one's hair again

definitions.meaning: to pull back or leave work for good
tire is an old word for attire or a headdress, so to tire hair a second time

explanation.definitionFit: To leave work or pull back is the first sense; to put a headdress (an archaic tire) on once more is the second.

clue.text: Sword waved about at hogmanay, without 10 shortly

indicators.note: waved about means the letters are tossed into a new order
without says some letters are taken away from the pool

parts.note: the answer at 10 across is a US state whose postal abbreviation is MO

explanation.surface: A blade brandished at the Scottish New Year, minus a brief American visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogmanay is the Scottish New Year's Eve. Take MO (Missouri, the answer to 10, abbreviated) out of AT HOGMANAY and rearrange what is left, ATHGANAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved Turkish sabre without a guard, a type of blade.
